sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.1 model card
sources.evidence: Exact v25.08 card identifies mistral-medium-2508, August 12, 2025, Premier status, nominal 128k context, text/image input and text output tooltips, function calling and document QnA. The card is deprecated and identifies Medium 3.5 as its replacement.

sources.title: Mistral documentation model data: exact Medium 3.1 object
sources.evidence: The object named Mistral Medium 3.1 has slug mistral-medium-3-1-25-08, API identifier mistral-medium-2508, type Premier, an empty weights array, contextLength 128k, input text/image, output text, and function-calling/document-qna features. It has no parameter or architecture specification. It records deprecation 2026-05-22 and retirement 2026-08-31.

sources.title: Mistral changelog: August 12, 2025
sources.evidence: Explicitly records the release of Mistral Medium 3.1, mistral-medium-2508, on August 12 in the 2025 chronology, separately from Medium 3 in May 2025 and Medium 3.5 in April 2026.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3 family legal and lifecycle documentation
sources.evidence: Names Medium 3.1 as an August 12, 2025 update within the Medium 3 model lifecycle. The embedded Technical Documentation content says documentation for 3.0 and subsequent 3.1/3.5 updates is still being prepared. Its Active lifecycle label conflicts with the inference card's deprecation data; it does not establish endpoint operation.

sources.title: Mistral known limitations: context windows
sources.evidence: Lists Medium 3.1 separately from 3.5 with a 128k-token context, including input and output. No token-exact integer is supplied for 3.1.

sources.title: Mistral Document AI QnA
sources.evidence: Explains Document QnA as OCR extraction followed by language-model analysis and shows PDF document_url requests. This distinguishes PDF service support from the model card's native text/image modalities.

sources.title: Phoenix-VL 1.5 Medium Technical Report
sources.evidence: May 2026 Mistral-coauthored report: section 1.1 starts from a Mistral Medium 3.1 base checkpoint. Its abstract assigns 123B parameters to Phoenix; sections 3.1-3.2 describe Phoenix's decoder-only Transformer and 2B ViT. Section 5.2 preserves the multimodal backbone during continued pretraining, while section 5.3 extends Phoenix's context. It does not directly state the production Medium 3.1 total/active counts or unchanged complete architecture/dimensions.

sources.title: Mistral model selection guide with Medium 3.1 query
sources.evidence: The live comparison renders Medium 3.5 despite the Medium 3.1 query. Its 128B total/active figures therefore do not support this record. The later official Medium 3.5 Hugging Face card was also checked and attributes dense 128B only to 3.5.

sources.title: Mistral commercial terms of service
sources.evidence: Current commercial terms grant limited product access and reserve Mistral's ownership of its products and underlying model materials. Together with the exact model's Premier classification and absence of distributed weights, this supports a descriptive proprietary classification, not a named open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenRouter exact Mistral Medium 3.1 endpoints
sources.evidence: Exact model ID mistralai/mistral-medium-3.1 has three endpoints explicitly naming provider Mistral, each publishing context_length 131072 and support for tools/tool_choice. This is primary evidence of the serving-provider configuration, not an independent measurement of the native model limit.

sources.title: Mistral Medium 3.5 128B model card
sources.evidence: Later sibling card identifies Medium 3.1 as a predecessor but reports dense 128B and configurable reasoning for Medium 3.5 only; these specifications are not transferred to 3.1.

name.note: Exact name and dated API identity match the frozen record.

developer.note: Retains the catalog's normalized label for Mistral AI.

family.note: The developer places 3.1 within the Medium 3 lifecycle.

release_date.note: Explicit original release date; OpenRouter's August 13 listing date is later.

open_weights.note: Exact model is Premier with no distributed weights; 3.5's open release is a different revision.

license.note: Descriptive commercial classification; no specific public weight-license identifier is established.

parameters_b.note: No exact production-2508 total is disclosed in the reviewed primary material. Phoenix's 123B derivative and Medium 3.5's 128B are not exact-model disclosures.

active_parameters_b.note: No exact-model active count is reported; neither derivative totals nor 3.5's explicitly labeled active count establish 3.1's value.

architecture.note: Exact-name searches covered later first-party cards, training and interpretability research. Phoenix provides indirect Transformer evidence, but no explicit unchanged-architecture statement for production 2508; density and routing are not established.

context_window.note: Retained as the exact hosted capacity published for Mistral's Medium 3.1 endpoints by OpenRouter. Mistral's native documentation says only nominal 128k; it does not independently establish a token-exact bound.

modalities.note: Remove PDF from native model modalities: the documented PDF QnA service combines OCR preprocessing with model analysis.

reasoning.note: The exact model lists text output and no dedicated reasoning control, but absence is insufficient to verify a categorical false. 3.5's explicit reasoning mode cannot be transferred.

tool_call.note: Exact card and serving endpoints explicitly support function calling.

description.value: Mistral's August 2025 multimodal model for text and image inputs, text responses, structured outputs, and function calling.
description.note: Replaces broad generic multilingual/reasoning copy with exact documented capabilities.

patch.description: Mistral's August 2025 multimodal model for text and image inputs, text responses, structured outputs, and function calling.
patch.notes: Exact revision: mistral-medium-2508. Context 131072 is the hosted capacity published by OpenRouter for its Mistral-provider endpoints; Mistral's native card states nominal 128k without an exact integer. Native inputs are text and images; PDF QnA uses OCR preprocessing. Total parameters, active parameters and exact production architecture remain unresolved. The Mistral-coauthored Phoenix report describes a 123B derivative of a Medium 3.1 base checkpoint, without explicitly establishing unchanged dimensions for the production model. Medium 3.5 specifications are not transferred. No dedicated reasoning mode was verified. The Mistral card is deprecated, and its model data records retirement on 2026-08-31; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Confirmed exact identity, August 12 release, proprietary closed weights and function calling. Retained 131072 strictly as the documented Mistral-provider hosted context, distinguished from native nominal 128k. Removed native PDF input, cleared the insufficiently supported reasoning=false assertion, replaced generic description and added primary provenance. Parameter counts remain undisclosed in exact-model evidence; architecture remains unverified after checking later model cards, comparison data and the Mistral-coauthored Phoenix training report.
